speckit:spec.description:
# Feature Specification: Remote MCP Server with HTTP Streaming, BTP Deployment, and Per-User Authentication

**Feature**: `053-remote-mcp-multitenant`
**Product Project**: `Informatica MDM MCP Server`
**Created**: 2026-04-27
**Status**: Draft

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-04-29

* Q: Which mechanism will the server use to obtain a user-scoped Informatica IDS-SESSION-ID for each authenticated MCP user? -> A: Federated SSO + token exchange via SAP IAS.
* Q: Which BTP runtime should be the deployment target? -> A: SAP BTP Cloud Foundry (Node.js buildpack).
* Q: Where do per-user IAS refresh tokens and Informatica IDS-SESSION-IDs live? -> A: In-memory per app instance with sticky routing.
* Q: Long-term status of stdio transport? -> A: Keep stdio for local development only.
* Q: How do MCP clients become OAuth clients of the server? -> A: Pre-registered clients in SAP IAS with OIDC discovery.

## Functional Requirements (excerpt)

* FR-001: HTTP Streamable transport in production.
* FR-007: Authenticate users against SAP IAS via OIDC.
* FR-009: Per-user secrets in process memory only; no persistence.
* FR-011b: Cloud Foundry route stickiness via JSESSIONID.

## Success Criteria

* SC-001: New user reaches first authorised tool call within 5 minutes.
* SC-002: At least 10 distinct users connected concurrently with isolated state.

speckit:plan.title: [PLAN] 053: Implementation Plan
speckit:plan.description:
# Implementation Plan: Remote MCP Server with HTTP Streaming, BTP Deployment, and Per-User Auth

**Feature**: `053-remote-mcp-multitenant` | **Date**: 2026-04-29
**Product Project**: `Informatica MDM MCP Server`

## Summary

Add a Streamable HTTP transport to the existing Node.js MCP server so it can be deployed once on SAP BTP Cloud Foundry and serve many users concurrently. Each user authenticates via SAP IAS (OIDC); the server exchanges the IAS assertion for a per-user Informatica IDS-SESSION-ID via IDMC's IAS federation trust.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.7, Node.js 20 LTS
**Primary Dependencies**: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.12, hono, zod, openid-client, pino.
**Storage**: None. All per-user state is in-memory.
**Testing**: vitest. New tests cover HTTP transport, IAS OIDC flow, IDMC federation token exchange.
**Target Platform**: SAP BTP Cloud Foundry (Node.js buildpack).

## Constitution Check

All 10 principles pass with one accepted deviation (P6 MELT — Metrics and Traces deferred to v1.1, ADR-053-002 documents the deviation).

## Phases

0. Research — IAS<->IDMC federation, MCP Streamable HTTP semantics, CF sticky routing.
1. Design & Contracts — entities, HTTP endpoints, quickstart guide.
2. Tasks — decomposed into 50 tasks across 8 milestones.

speckit:research.title: [RESEARCH] 053: Technical Research
speckit:research.description:
# Technical Research: Remote MCP Server with HTTP Streaming, BTP Deployment, and Per-User Auth

**Feature**: `053-remote-mcp-multitenant`

## R-1: SAP IAS to Informatica IDMC Federation

**Decision**: Use the OIDC + SAML 2.0 Bearer Assertion Grant (RFC 7522) federation pattern.

**Rationale**: This is the IDMC-supported pattern for enterprise SSO. Satisfies FR-008 (no raw passwords), SC-003 (audit log shows real user), and SC-009 (no password ever crosses the MCP boundary).

**Alternatives considered**: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693, IDMC does not expose endpoints); IDMC native OIDC client (undocumented API); IDMC personal access tokens (high onboarding friction).

## R-2: MCP Streamable HTTP Transport in TS SDK

**Decision**: Use StreamableHTTPServerTransport from @modelcontextprotocol/sdk.

## R-3: SAP BTP Cloud Foundry Sticky Session Routing

**Decision**: Use the JSESSIONID cookie. The CF gorouter natively recognises this cookie name and routes subsequent requests with the same value to the same backend instance.

speckit:data-model.title: [DATA-MODEL] 053: Entity Definitions
speckit:data-model.description:
# Data Model: Remote MCP Server with HTTP Streaming, BTP Deployment, and Per-User Auth

**Feature**: `053-remote-mcp-multitenant`

This document defines all in-process entities introduced or modified by this feature. There is no persistent data store; all entities live in process memory.

## E1: McpSession

A long-lived MCP session bound to one authenticated user. Created on the first authenticated MCP request, destroyed on logout, idle timeout, or app instance shutdown. Pinned to one CF instance via the JSESSIONID cookie.

## E2: EndUserIdentity

The authenticated end-user identity resolved from SAP IAS (HTTP transport) or environment variables (stdio transport).

## E3: InformaticaUserSession

The per-user IDMC IDS-SESSION-ID derived from the user's IAS identity.

## E4: RegisteredMcpClient

A pre-registered OAuth client representing one MCP client product (e.g., Claude Desktop). Loaded at server startup from configuration.

## E5: ToolInvocationRecord

A per-tool-call audit-relevant record emitted to the structured log stream.

speckit:contract.title: [CONTRACT] 053: API Contract
speckit:contract.description:
# API Contract: Remote MCP Server with HTTP Streaming, BTP Deployment, and Per-User Auth

**Feature**: `053-remote-mcp-multitenant`

This issue defines all HTTP endpoints exposed by the MCP server in HTTP transport mode.

## Endpoint Summary

| Method | Path | Purpose | Auth | Streaming |
|--------|------|---------|------|-----------|
| GET | /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server | RFC 8414 OAuth metadata | Public | No |
| GET | /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource | RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata | Public | No |
| POST | /mcp | MCP client->server JSON-RPC requests | Bearer | SSE upgrade |
| GET | /mcp | MCP server->client SSE stream | Bearer | Yes |
| DELETE | /mcp | Terminate an MCP session | Bearer | No |
| GET | /health | Liveness probe | Public | No |
| GET | /ready | Readiness probe | Public | No |

## Error Code Surface

AUTH_NO_TOKEN (401), AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN (401), AUTH_UNKNOWN_CLIENT (401), IDMC_FEDERATION_FAILED (502), IDMC_USER_DISABLED (403), MCP_SESSION_NOT_FOUND (404).

speckit:quickstart.title: [QUICKSTART] 053: Integration Guide
speckit:quickstart.description:
# Quickstart: Remote MCP Server with HTTP Streaming, BTP Deployment, and Per-User Auth

**Feature**: `053-remote-mcp-multitenant`

This document covers four audiences: end users (signing in), MCP-client integrators (registering a new client), operations (deploying), and developers (running locally).

## 1. End-User Quickstart

Prerequisite: Operations has already deployed the server and registered your MCP client product in SAP IAS. You should have the MCP server URL and a valid SAP IAS account.

Steps (Claude Desktop example):

1. Open Claude Desktop -> Settings -> Connectors.
2. Add a new MCP server: paste the URL.
3. Claude Desktop fetches /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, discovers your IAS tenant, and opens a browser for sign-in.
4. Sign in to SAP IAS. Approve the consent screen.
5. Browser redirects back to Claude Desktop, which receives an OAuth access token.
6. Try a tool: ask Claude to list the materials you can see.

Expected first-tool-call time: under 5 minutes from a clean install (per SC-001).

speckit:constitution.title: [CONSTITUTION] Project Constitution
speckit:constitution.description:
# Application Development Constitution

## Principles

### Principle 1: Test-First Development

All production code MUST be accompanied by automated tests written before or alongside the implementation. The project follows the test pyramid model: Unit tests (70%), Integration tests (20%), End-to-end tests (10%).

Coverage targets: Business logic and algorithms (90% minimum), Infrastructure/glue code (70% minimum), Critical paths (100%).

### Principle 2: Security by Design

Security MUST be addressed from the design phase, not retrofitted. All code MUST comply with the OWASP Top 10 and follow shift-left security practices. Pre-commit security scanning is MANDATORY.

### Principle 3: Simplicity and Maintainability

Code MUST favor simplicity over cleverness. KISS, YAGNI, DRY, SOLID principles apply.

### Principle 4: Clean Architecture and Separation of Concerns

Applications MUST separate business logic from infrastructure, frameworks, and external services. 12-Factor compliant. ADRs for significant architectural decisions.

### Principle 5: Continuous Integration and Automated Quality Gates

All code changes MUST pass through an automated CI/CD pipeline before reaching production. No direct commits to main. PR workflow MANDATORY.

**Version**: 1.2.0
**Ratified**: 2026-02-07
**Last Amended**: 2026-02-08
